    Opposite split-basic ray categories #

    Reverse the BGRS unit-ray product through the primitive-projective equivalence between a split-basic algebra and its opposite. The resulting equivalence of ray categories reverses irreducible ray-quiver arrows and sends singular pairs to singular pairs.

    IsIrreducibleRayMorphism f

    A fully faithful functor reflects irreducibility. Essential surjectivity is not needed in this direction because a factorization of the original morphism already maps to a factorization through an object in the image.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.SplitBasicIdempotents.op_mem_twoSidedEndomorphismSpan_iff {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] {ι : Type x} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : SplitBasicIdempotents) [Module.Finite k A] {X Y : S.ProjectiveCategory} (f g : X ⟶ Y) :
    g.op ∈ twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k f.op ↔ g ∈ twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k f

    Membership in a principal two-sided Hom span is invariant under categorical opposite. The endpoint actions exchange sides under op.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.SplitBasicIdempotents.twoSidedEndomorphismSpan_op_eq_top_iff {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] {ι : Type x} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : SplitBasicIdempotents) [Module.Finite k A] {X Y : S.ProjectiveCategory} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k f.op = ⊤ ↔ twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k f = ⊤

    Opposing a primitive-projective morphism preserves the property of generating its whole Hom space as a two-sided endpoint-endomorphism bimodule.
